newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open little changed.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open little changed Thursday, with silver leading the recovery from Wednesday's sell off.
Palladium was little changed overnight despite news Russian central bank representatives are to visit Japan next week to begin negotiations on resuming platinum group metal sales to Japan.
COMEX June gold was called unchanged to off $0.20 from Wednesday's settlement of $343.30 an ounce after trading from $344.10 to $343.30 on ACCESS.
COMEX warehouse gold stocks slipped 64 ounces to 1,032,318 ounces Wednesday.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $341.00/50 early compared to the London morning fix of $341.20 and the New York close Wednesday of $341.00/50.
The Islamic holiday of Id is seen limiting gold demand in the Mid-East this week, but Indian gold demand is seen gaining a seasonal boost in coming weeks from the second Indian wedding season.
COMEX May silver was called up 2.0 to 4.0 cents from the previous close of $4.77.
COMEX silver stocks fell 648,339 ounces to 189,888,933 ounces Wednesday.
NYMEX July platinum was called unchanged to $0.50 firmer from Wednesday's close of $371.80, with NYMEX June palladium called unchanged to off $0.50 from yesterday's $151.00.

In the bullion market, spot palladium prices were little changed by news overnight Russian central bankers would resume negotiations on a Russian/Japanese supply contract for platinum group metals next week.
Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Chubais also said Russia would adopt a new approach to raising revenue by sales of precious metals, privatizations and equity issues.
